title: Picking fruit for a smoothie: when order does not matter
examples: What is the difference between permutations and combinations?
How many ways can you choose 3 from 5?
Why do you divide by 3 factorial?

explain.say: You have 5 fruits: mango, banana, guava, papaya and pineapple. You pick 3 for a smoothie. How many different smoothies can you make? First, look at the left side, where order matters, like medals in a race.

draw.text: Picking fruit for a smoothie: when order does not matter

explain.say: For medals: 5 choices for gold, 4 for silver, 3 for bronze. 5 times 4 times 3 is 60 ways. Mango, banana, guava is different from guava, banana, mango, because the winners swap places. Does order matter in a smoothie?
Not at all! Look at the right side. Mango, banana, guava blended tastes the same in any order. So many of those 60 lists are really the same smoothie.

How many times is each smoothie counted? The 3 fruits can be ordered in 3 times 2 times 1, which is 6 ways. So divide: 60 over 6 is 10 smoothies. Choosing without order is called a combination, written 5 choose 3.
Well done! Lotteries use combinations: picking 6 numbers out of 49 gives almost 14 million choices. That is why winning is so rare. Challenge: how many smoothies with 2 fruits from the 5?

faq.q: What is the difference between permutations and combinations?
faq.a: In a permutation the order matters, like a race podium. In a combination it does not, like choosing fruits for a smoothie or players for a team.

faq.q: How many ways can you choose 3 from 5?
faq.a: 10 ways. There are 60 ordered lists, and each group of 3 appears in 6 orders, so 60 divided by 6 is 10.

faq.q: Why do you divide by 3 factorial?
faq.a: Each group of 3 can be arranged in 3 factorial, which is 6, orders. Counting ordered lists counts each group 6 times, so you divide by 6.

faq.q: What is the formula for combinations?
faq.a: n choose r equals n factorial divided by r factorial times n minus r factorial. For 5 choose 3: 120 over 6 times 2, which is 10.

faq.q: How many smoothies with 2 fruits from 5?
faq.a: 5 times 4 is 20 ordered pairs, and each pair is counted twice, so 10 smoothies. It matches 5 choose 3, because choosing 2 to use is like choosing 3 to leave out.

facts: The number of ways to choose r items from n, ignoring order, is n!/(r!(n − r)!).
Choosing 6 numbers from 49 gives 13 983 816 possible combinations.
